content.title: Why did Rocky Carroll leave NCIS? The real reason behind Director Vance's shocking fate in the 500th Episode
content.text: Actualizado 24/03/2026 - 21:25 CDTFans of NCIS were caught completely off guard when the show made one of its boldest decisions yet: killing off Director Leon Vance in its milestone 500th episode.To watch this video, agree to share video information with third partiesAgree|More infoIn Tuesday's episode, the NCIS team was left in shock when the Department of Defense ordered the agency to shut down. However, Director Vance, played by Rocky Carroll, stood firmly by his team as they raced against the clock to prove the innocence of a petty officer accused of murder. In the end, Vance managed to clear her name and restore NCIS, but the victory came at a high cost: he lost his life after being shot by a corrupt agent.The exit of Carroll, who had been part of the series for nearly two decades, wasn't due to behind-the-scenes drama or a sudden departure. Instead, it was a creative choice - one designed to make a lasting impact.A creative decision, not a personal exitAccording to Carroll, the decision to end Vance's story had been in the works for years. but producers hesitated because of how important the character had become. In fact, executive producer Steven D. Binder chose Vance for this shocking twist precisely because of his weight in the story.Carroll explained it this way in an interview with Variety."It was a very macabre compliment, but he said, 'Because of who you are, Rocky, and because of what you brought to the character, we've been talking about killing off Vance for the last 10 years. This idea didn't just come about in 2025. We've been thinking about killing this character or having this character meet some sort of untimely death for over a decade. But we couldn't because it was you.' And I think they figured, 'Look, 23 seasons in, who knows how much more time we have. If we don't do it now, there may not be a season that allows us to do something of this magnitude, because we're in overtime here.'Why Vance had to dieUnlike other major characters in NCIS - who often leave the door open for returns - Vance's ending was intentionally final."The middle of November, I believe, is when our executive producer, our showrunner Steve Binder, came to me after a day of filming and said, 'So the 500th episode of NCIS is coming up and we want to do something big. We want to do something that shocks our loyal viewers and just really turns the NCIS universe upside down.'", he told People. "And I was like, 'Oh, wow, that sounds great. Tell me more.'Carroll himself initially questioned the decision, but the 500th episode needed something bigger. And that "something" was a definitive, emotional goodbye.Rocky Carroll was at peace with the exitDespite the surprise for fans, Carroll says he had time to process the decision after learning about it months in advance. Far from frustration, the actor framed his departure as a rare achievement in Hollywood."I've been able to kind of come full circle with it. And I really think it's a great episode. I'm not just saying this to be a team player, but if you've gotta send a character off, what a way to go," he told Variety. "I've been a character on this series for 18 years. Most Hollywood careers don't last 18 years. So to be able to play one character on one of the most popular shows in the world for 18 seasons, that's the equivalent of living to be 105.Not a full goodbyeEven though Vance's story has ended, Carroll isn't completely leaving NCIS.He remains actively involved behind the camera and has already returned to direct new episodes of the series.And given NCIS' long history of bringing characters back through flashbacks or visions, the door isn't entirely closed.
